content: The test image shows a corn ear with extensive mold growth — grayish-white with some pinkish/reddish coloration. This is clearly an ear rot. Let me view reference images for the ear rot classes and a couple others.

**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Corn **ear** (not leaf/stalk)
- Extensive grayish-white/chalky mold covering the entire ear
- Some pinkish/reddish tones mixed in the mold
- Dried, papery husks pulled back
- Kernels visible under complete fungal coverage
- Field setting, late-season appearance

**Candidate comparison:**
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia** ✓ — White/chalky mold covering entire ear, dried husks, bleached appearance — matches very well
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella** — Reference showed dark/brown husks and stalk discoloration, not the white chalky coverage seen here
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus** — Greenish/olive mold on yellow kernels — doesn't match
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma** — Dark teal/green mold — doesn't match
- **Fusarium** — Patchy pink/white on individual kernels, not complete coverage — doesn't match
- All leaf/stalk diseases — clearly wrong tissue type

The complete white-gray chalky mold enveloping the entire ear with dried bleached husks is the hallmark of Diplodia ear rot (*Stenocarpella maydis*), which starts at the base of the ear and progresses upward with dense white mycelium.
